points: The test: can every agent find the right file in any repo without being told where it is?
Three questions decide where a file goes: is it current truth or history? does it die when the work ships? does every repo have one?

Layout: CLAUDE.md under 200 lines with AGENTS.md as a symlink; .claude/rules/; tokens/tokens.json; docs/design (DESIGN.md, mockups, reference), docs/decisions, docs/debts with notes.md, docs/plans; scripts/shoot; shots/ gitignored.
Path-scoped rules (paths: frontmatter in .claude/rules/) load only when Claude touches matching files; ~/.claude/rules/ applies in every project. Your installer doesn't land a rules folder yet.
Tokens in the W3C Design Tokens format (stable since 2025.10), generated into CSS and Swift with Style Dictionary or Terrazzo.
No history in the tree: delete superseded decisions, since git keeps them.
Don't restructure code into apps/ and packages/: one app with a backend gains little from a monorepo layout.
q_max keeps design truth in six places (design/, specs/, docs/design.md, docs/rules/, src/styles.md, brand/). Merging them into docs/design/DESIGN.md is a copy-delete, which fits the cull's own rule.
Folders sort volume but don't reduce it: q_max's 759 debts and 560 decisions stay unreadable until they're culled.

One home, then variants (o11, topic t18): claude-settings holds the shared ideas and shared tools (scripts/shoot, skills); each repo holds its own concrete design (tokens, components) in one home and points at the ideas instead of restating them.
summary: One layout for every repo, checked against current practice.
title: Folder layout and conventions
